sentences.text: Microraptor is a small genus of four-winged dromaeosaurid dinosaurs, a group of theropods. It possessed long pennaceous feathers on its arms, tail, and legs, giving it a unique appearance.
A new specimen revealed that the animal probably had glossy-black iridescent plumage.
However, a new specimen suggests the nuchal crest seen in the holotype may be a taphonomic artifact rather than a true feature.
The holotype of M. gui measured 77 cm in length, had a wingspan of 88 to 94 cm, and weighed between 0.5 and 1.4 kg.
The genus Microraptor was described by Xu and colleagues in 2000 based on well-preserved fossils found in Liaoning, China.
The initial Microraptor specimen was a chimeric patchwork of different species assembled from fossils smuggled from China to the USA.
Xu Xing later published a description of the tail specimen, naming it Microraptor zhaoianus.
Xu and colleagues suggested in 2003 that basal dromaeosaurs were likely small, lived in trees, and could glide.
Evidence from gut contents indicates the animal ate mammal prey with an estimated snout-to-vent length of 80 mm and a mass of 13–43 g.

In 2003, Xu Xing described a Microraptor specimen as a "four-winged dinosaur" and speculated it could glide using all four limbs. Later studies suggest Microraptor may have been capable of powered flight.
The type species of Microraptor is Microraptor zhaoianus, and the genus includes the species M. gui and M. hanqingi.
Cryptovolans pauli and Tetrapterornis are associated with Microraptor, and Cryptovolans is usually considered a synonym of Microraptor.

Microraptor lived during the early Cretaceous, specifically the Aptian stage, between 125 and 120 million years ago. It is a genus of three valid dromaeosaurid theropod dinosaur species that lived during the Early Cretaceous, between 125 and 113 million years ago in the Aptian stage, in what is now Asia.
All Microraptor species come from the Jiufotang Formation of the early Cretaceous Aptian stage, approximately 120 million years ago.

Senter and colleagues in 2004 suggested that Cryptovolans pauli and Microraptor gui are synonyms of Microraptor zhaoianus due to individual variation. Some researchers accept Microraptor gui as a distinct species based on a 2013 specimen.

It was originally hypothesized that Microraptor was an arboreal glider because its hindwings would have hindered ground running. Some paleontologists suggest that feathered dinosaurs may have used their wings to parachute from trees to ambush prey as a precursor to gliding or flight.
